as_told.title: The Telepathy Tapes: nonverbal children communicating on the hill

plain: Some autistic people who cannot speak are said to share a telepathic link with one caregiver, usually their mother, so that the caregiver's thoughts reach them without words. The story comes from The Telepathy Tapes, a 2024 series built on the work of the researcher Diane Hennacy Powell. Matthew Pines, a commentator on national security, tells Michels it is a "remarkable story of dozens of nonverbal individuals with autism" who report such a connection, and he credits Powell. The scientist Don Hoffman says he has seen studies where an autistic child "who can hardly even control their body is able to read what's in their mother's mind," and that some of the experiment designs "seemed pretty rigorous." The retired Navy admiral Tim Gallaudet points to Powell's work with autistic patients over the 2010s and 2020s rather than to the series. Kurt McConnell, a former Senate staffer, goes further and says these people "connect with each other across vast distances." Michels himself describes the children as communing together on a kind of "hill." If true, it would mean minds can link directly, which some of these tellers tie to how non-human beings might communicate.
